title: Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) Cycle
path: Quality Improvement in Healthcare and Patient Safety
Improvement Plans and Tests of Change

headings.title: Introduction to Quality Improvement in Nursing
headings.content: Quality improvement in nursing focuses on structured methods to monitor, evaluate, and upgrade healthcare services. Rather than accepting routine challenges as permanent, nurses use systematic approaches to fix broken workflows. Safe patient care, reduction of medication errors, and efficient use of hospital resources depend heavily on these ongoing assessment frameworks.

headings.title: Overview of the PDSA Cycle
headings.content: The Plan-Do-Study-Act cycle serves as a shorthand framework for testing small-scale changes in clinical practice. Walter Shewhart originally developed the concept, and W. Edwards Deming later popularized it for industrial and healthcare settings. By breaking large problems into manageable trials, nursing teams can test interventions safely before committing to permanent unit-wide policies.

headings.title: Step 1: The Plan Phase
headings.content:
Planning requires a clear statement of the objective, predictions about the outcome, and a defined data collection strategy. Nurses must answer three fundamental questions: What are we trying to accomplish? How will we know that a change is an improvement? What change can we make that will result in improvement?

- **Objective setting**: Defining the exact goal of the intervention.
- **Prediction**: Stating what the team expects to happen when the change is introduced.
- **Data plan**: Deciding who will collect metrics, when, and using what tool.

headings.title: Step 2: The Do Phase
headings.content: During the Do phase, the team executes the intervention on a small scale. Data collection begins immediately to capture problems, surprises, and initial observations. Unforeseen operational barriers often surface here, making real-time note-taking critical for success.

headings.title: Step 3: The Study Phase
headings.content: The study phase compares the gathered data against the original predictions made during planning. The team analyzes trends, looks for unintended consequences, and summarizes what they learned. Skipping this step leads to blind adoption of unverified practices.

headings.title: Step 4: The Act Phase
headings.content:
Based on what was learned in the study phase, the team decides on the next course of action. This decision typically follows the 'adopt, adapt, or abandon' rule:

- **Adopt**: The test worked well, so the team rolls out the change on a larger scale.
- **Adapt**: The test showed promise but needs modifications before further testing.
- **Abandon**: The test failed to improve outcomes, so the team stops the intervention and tries a different approach.

headings.title: Applying PDSA in Nigerian Healthcare Settings
headings.content: Implementing quality improvement cycles in Nigerian hospitals requires navigating local challenges such as erratic power supply, resource scarcity, and high patient volumes. Successful nursing leaders involve frontline staff—including auxiliary nurses and records officers—because ownership ensures sustainability. Small tests of change prove valuable here, as they do not require massive budgets to demonstrate better ways of organizing patient care.
